A stress-beat diagram for the neutral sentence "Tunde bought a new bicycle." Each word is written along a horizontal line with a circle above it: medium circles above "Tunde", "bought" and "new"; a very small circle above "a"; and the largest, dark-orange circle above the last content word "bicycle",. Medium circles are and the small circle "unstressed function word". Clean flat educational illustration, white background, soft colours.

A "spotlight" diagram. The sentence "My father bought a new car yesterday" is written six times in a column. In each row, one word is written larger, bold and in dark orange with a small spotlight shining on it (row 1 "MY", row 2 "FATHER", row 3 "BOUGHT", row 4 "NEW", row 5 "CAR", row 6 "YESTERDAY"), and the rest of the sentence is in pale grey. To the right of each row is a speech bubble with the matching question: "Your friend's father?", "Your mother?", "Did he sell one?", "A used car?", "A new bus?", "Last week?". Clean flat educational illustration, white background.

Two intonation curves drawn as smooth lines above two sentences. Top: "I bought a new CAR." with a flat line that rises slightly and then falls steeply on "CAR"; a down-arrow at the end; label "Falling tune (Tune 1): statements, wh-questions, commands". Bottom: "Are you COMING?" with a flat low line that rises steeply on "COMING"; an up-arrow at the end; label "Rising tune (Tune 2): yes/no questions, uncertainty". The stressed word in each sentence is in dark orange capitals. Clean flat educational illustration, white background, soft blue lines.
